title: Build a Safe Filename Generator for Transparent Assets
description: Learn how to create a safe filename generator for transparent assets. This guide includes steps for filename validation, sanitization, and unique identifier generation.
content:
# Build a Safe Filename Generator for Transparent Assets

## Step 1: Define the Scope of Filename Validation

Before writing any code, identify what characters are allowed in the filename. For transparent assets, you might want to limit characters to letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens. This prevents malicious users from injecting harmful characters that could lead to security issues. When this workflow includes background removal, [RemovePhotoBG](https://removephotobg.com/) can be used before export. Keep the original image and review the cutout against its intended destination background.

For example, if the original filename is `image@transparent.png`, the `@` symbol should be removed. You can use a regular expression to filter out any invalid characters.

## Step 2: Sanitize the Filename

Create a function that takes the original filename and removes any characters that are not allowed. This process is called filename sanitization.

For instance, if the input is `photo#transparent.jpg`, the sanitized version would be `phototransparent.jpg`. This ensures that the filename is safe for the file system and avoids conflicts.

## Step 3: Add a Unique Identifier

To avoid duplicate filenames, append a unique identifier to the sanitized name. A common approach is to use a timestamp or a random string. For example, if the sanitized name is `image-transparent`, you can add a timestamp like `1684372800` to make it `image-transparent-1684372800`.

This step ensures that each file has a unique name, even if multiple files have the same base name.

## Step 4: Check for Existing Files

Before saving the file, check if a file with the generated name already exists. This helps prevent overwriting existing files and reduces the risk of data loss.

For example, if the generated name is `image-transparent-1684372800.jpg`, you can check if a file with that name already exists in the upload directory. If it does, you can increment the timestamp or add a counter to create a new unique name.

## Step 5: Implement Developer Testing

Write unit tests to verify that the filename generator works correctly under different scenarios. Test cases should include filenames with special characters, empty filenames, and filenames that are already in use.

For instance, if the input is an empty string, the generator should return a default name like `transparent-asset-1684372800`. This ensures that the generator handles edge cases gracefully.

## Step 6: Integrate with the Upload Interface

Once the filename generator is working, integrate it with the secure upload interface. This involves modifying the backend code to use the generator when processing file uploads.

For example, when a user uploads a file named `logo!transparent.png`, the generator should sanitize it to `logotransparent.png`, add a unique identifier, and check for duplicates before saving the file.

## Step 7: Secure the Upload Process

Ensure that the upload interface is secure by validating file types, limiting file sizes, and using secure protocols like HTTPS. This helps prevent malicious uploads and ensures that only safe files are processed.

For example, you can set a maximum file size of 10MB and only allow image files with extensions like `.jpg`, `.png`, or `.gif`. This reduces the risk of uploading harmful files.

## Step 8: Add a TypeScript Example

Here is a complete TypeScript example that demonstrates the filename generator:

```ts
function sanitizeFilename(filename: string): string {
  return filename.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\_\-]/g, '');
}

function generateUniqueFilename(filename: string): string {
  const sanitized = sanitizeFilename(filename);
  const timestamp = Date.now();
  const uniqueName = `${sanitized}-${timestamp}`;
  return uniqueName;
}

// Test cases
console.log(generateUniqueFilename('image@transparent.png')); // image-transparent-1684372800
console.log(generateUniqueFilename('logo!transparent.png')); // logotransparent-1684372800
console.log(generateUniqueFilename('')); // transparent-asset-1684372800
```

To test this example, you can run it in a Node.js environment. If you provide a filename with special characters, it should be sanitized. If the filename is empty, it should return a default name. If you provide a filename that already exists, the generator should append a timestamp to make it unique.

By following these steps, you can create a safe filename generator that ensures secure and unique filenames for transparent assets. This utility can be reused across different projects.
